title: Charles II to the Duke of Hamilton, Aug-Sept 1650 (NRS GD406/1/10573-10576)

documents.shelfmark: NRS GD406/1/10573-10576 (Hamilton Red Book ii nos. 156-159); printed in the 1766 Account and Camden Society 1880

plaintext.source: Printed with the figures undeciphered (1766 Account; Gardiner 1880; HMC 1887)

transcription.source: 1766 Account of the Preservation of King Charles II, collated with Gardiner's Camden edition 1880 (collate.py)
transcription.notes: Four letters attacked as one set; the two printed witnesses differ at five places.

system.summary: Small numeric nomenclator, groups 3-384, probably letters below about 90 and words and names above.
system.sibling_key: Key sheets NRS GD406/1/2197 (5 items, c 1645) located, not obtained
system.notes: Structure is a guess from Charles II's 1648 Swan cipher and the Nicholas 1650 letter.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Camden 1880 Hamilton Papers: prints decipherments of 1647-48 only, no key; Burnet has nothing.
Located the key sheets NRS GD406/1/2197 in the NRS catalogue.
102 groups, 67 distinct: too short for ciphertext-only attack.

outcome.method_basis: The cipher groups survive only in two printed witnesses (1766 Account, Camden 1880) and are too short for a ciphertext-only attack; the probable key sheets, NRS GD406/1/2197, are available only on site.
